competitors.title: Maxim AI - Evaluations Product Overview
key_points: Multi-level evaluation system: Session-level (entire conversations), Trace-level (single interactions), Span-level (specific components)
Pre-built evaluator library: AI evaluators (LLM-as-a-Judge), Statistical (BLEU, ROUGE, WER, TER), Programmatic (validJson, validURL)
Custom evaluators: AI (configurable prompts/models), Programmatic (JavaScript functions), API-based (external model endpoints), Human (annotators in the loop)
Online evaluations: real-time scoring of production interactions via auto-evaluation UI or SDK node-level evaluation
Offline evaluations: curated datasets, scenario simulations, and evaluators for pre-deployment benchmarking

competitors.title: Maxim AI - Agent Simulations
key_points: AI-powered simulations test agents across thousands of scenarios using user-defined metrics
Voice simulation with real-time native audio processing preserves emotion, tone, interruptions, and latency characteristics
Framework-agnostic simulation supports any agent stack via SDK, CLI, or direct integration
Automations integrate seamlessly with CI/CD workflows for regression testing
Last-mile human evaluation pipelines simplify and scale human-in-the-loop quality checks

competitors.title: What are Online Evaluations? - Maxim AI Blog
key_points: Online evaluations attach evaluators to traces, spans, generations, and retrievals to automatically score real production interactions in real-time
Three evaluation levels: Session (multi-turn conversation quality), Trace (individual response quality), Span (component-specific metrics like retrieval quality or tool usage)
Auto-evaluation via UI: configure evaluators, variable mapping, filter rules, and sampling without code changes
SDK node-level evaluation: attach evaluators and variables programmatically with 5-minute grace period for missing variables
Python and TypeScript SDK examples show integration with customer support agents and RAG systems

competitors.title: What are Offline Evaluations? - Maxim AI Blog
key_points: Offline evaluations use curated datasets, scenario simulations, and evaluators to benchmark prompts, workflows, and agents before deployment
Key concepts: Prompts (multi-turn with variables/model params), Prompt comparisons (side-by-side up to 5), No-code agent builder, HTTP endpoint workflows
Dataset properties: variables, expected tool calls, conversation history, expected steps, scenarios
Context sources expose RAG pipelines via simple endpoints for evaluation
Prompt Tools allow mimicking agentic flows with custom functions exposed to LLMs
Evaluator types: AI, Programmatic, Statistical, Human, API-based with pre-built options available from the store

competitors.title: Voice Simulation: Testing Voice Agents the Way Users Experience Them - Maxim AI Blog
key_points: Real-time native audio processing preserves timing, prosody, emotion, and interruptions as first-class inputs
STT→LLM→TTS pipeline has four fatal flaws: latency compounding (4-6s vs sub-2s required), emotional tone erasure, VAD guessing game, impossible interruptions
Built-in evaluations: sentiment analysis, user satisfaction, AI/user interruption detection, abrupt call termination, speech rate, latency, SNR, talk ratio
Role switching challenge solved with persistent physical persona anchoring and contextual grounding
Voice simulation connects to existing voice stacks (Twilio, Vapi) for realistic automated testing

competitors.title: Beyond the SDK: Why AI Teams Love HTTP Endpoint-Based Evals - Maxim AI Blog
key_points: HTTP Endpoint evals treat AI agents as black-box services, decoupling evaluation logic from source code
Multi-turn simulation support with {{simulation_id}} variable for session context across stateless APIs
Pre- and post-request scripts for dynamic payload manipulation and complex session logic
Vault and Environments for secure auth token management and staging/prod switching
Enterprise pattern: Global 500 utility company uses standardized HTTP evals as unified quality gateway across 'swarm of agents' from independent teams

angles: The three-layer QA lifecycle: Experiment (pre-deployment prompt iteration) → Simulate & Evaluate (offline agent testing) → Observe (online production monitoring) — and how Maxim unifies all three in one platform
Online vs offline evaluations: why you need both — offline catches regressions before deployment, online catches edge cases that testing couldn't simulate

Multi-level evaluation architecture: why session-level (conversation flow), trace-level (single responses), and span-level (component metrics like tool calls or retrievals) each catch different failure modes

Voice agent testing is fundamentally different from text chatbot testing — real-time audio, emotion, interruptions, and sub-2s latency requirements demand native audio processing, not STT→LLM→TTS pipelines

HTTP endpoint evals as a quality gateway: how decoupling evaluation from code enables cross-functional teams (PMs, domain experts) to run evaluations and creates standardized quality gates for enterprise 'swarms of agents'

Pre-built vs custom evaluators: LLM-as-a-Judge for subjective quality, statistical metrics for objective accuracy, programmatic checks for validation, and human-in-the-loop for nuanced edge cases — building a complete evaluation strategy

Dataset evolution as continuous practice: Maxim's approach to synthetic data generation, curation workflows, and dataset properties (expected tool calls, conversation history, scenarios) for realistic offline testing
From reactive troubleshooting to proactive quality management: how the shift from debugging production incidents to continuous pre-deployment evaluation transforms AI development velocity
